analysis.title: #GLOBALMARKETS WEEKLY WRAP-UP, November 14, 2026
key_insights: Wall Street had its first winning week since early October: S&P 500 +2.5% to 7,562 (+10.5% YTD), Nasdaq +2.3% (best week since August), Dow +2.1%. Gains faded Friday as chipmakers sold off.

Nvidia lost roughly 12% on the week (other pages cite about 11%, worst since April 2025) after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and its market value fell below $4trn. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The board is considering internal and external candidates. Polymarket gives Arm CEO Rene Haas a 33% chance of being the replacement, per the chart of the week.

The Nvidia story kept developing Friday: Bloomberg reported a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang procured smuggled AI chips for a Shanghai data center linked to Megaspeed, Commerce Secretary Lutnick agreed to testify before Congress, and interim CEO Kress reportedly pushed back on some of Huang's financing deals. The wrap notes Nvidia has acted as the AI ecosystem's lender of last resort.

Money stayed in AI but rotated away from Nvidia: AMD rose about 30%, Broadcom 24%, and the SOX had its best week since April. NVDA's valuation fell to its lowest in 13 years after six straight weekly declines, the longest losing streak in 14 years, which the wrap reads as a structural shift in the AI trade rather than a Huang-specific problem.

Treasuries sold off hard: the 10-year yield rose about 27bp to 5.13% (touched 5.17%, highest since October). The 2Y rose about 35bp, its biggest weekly jump since October 2024, and 5s30s flattened almost 13bp. The latest $42B 10-year auction had a bid-to-cover of 2.46 versus 2.77 prior and cleared at 5.02%, 1bp above the 5.01% expected.

October CPI rose 0.4% m/m with core at 0.3% for a third month. No annual rate was published, but estimates point to roughly 4%. PPI rose 0.3% m/m with annual wholesale inflation at 6.5%, the highest since 2022.

Fed pricing has moved to hikes: markets almost fully price a December hike from the current 3.75-4.00% range. Waller floated 50bp, Logan said the FOMC needs at least two more 25bp hikes, Bowman could back a December hike, and Daly and Hammack also lean toward further tightening. December prices a 10% chance of 50bp and January a 70% chance of another 25bp. After PPI, 2027 is priced 50/50 for 2 or 3 more hikes. The Bank of England hiked to 4.00% last week.

The dollar index hit its strongest level since April/May 2025 after its biggest two-day jump since June, breaking an 18-month range. EUR/USD fell toward 1.11 and USD/JPY briefly broke 160 on Thursday, prompting a warning from Japan's FX chief Mimura that moves were excessively rapid, which revives intervention risk.
Gold fell 4.7% on the week to about $3,874, its first close below $4,000 in months and lowest since early October 2025, as it traded as a real-rate asset. Silver lost 3.6% to just under $50.

Oil: Brent fell almost 6% to $92.57 early in the week and broke below $90 on Tuesday for the first time since August. It rebounded to around $96 by week-end as hopes for a US-Iran settlement faded. US gasoline fell below $4 a gallon. Trump said further strikes were highly unlikely, and reports said the US and Iran were considering an $8B deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz before Trump said Gulf states prefer the status quo.

AI-credit stress sits beneath the equity rally. CoreWeave beat and raised (Q3 revenue $3.66B vs $3.56B est, adjusted EBITDA $2.26B vs $2.05B est) but guided to about $1.1B of quarterly interest on $47B of debt, with $35-39B of 2026 capex and a $529M adjusted net loss. The stock rose 25% Wednesday. Chip CDS widened beyond hyperscaler CDS for the first time, and CCC spreads are 270bp wider in three months. BloombergNEF says data center builders face $13.4B of debt due starting next year, costing at least $380M more to refinance at today's rates.

Anthropic is targeting Nov 19-20 to list on Nasdaq under ANT, per WSJ. The valuation range is due early in the week and some investors are pushing for less than the $1.5T previously expected. Liquid implies $1.69T. Microsoft fell 2% after Anthropic launched Claude Sheets and Claude Meetings.

Bitcoin fell to about $71,400 Thursday, its lowest close since mid-August and down almost 6% on the week, then slid below $70,000 Friday, back under its 200-day moving average. Ether lost about 10%. MSCI will remove Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes on Nov 30, which could trigger about $2.8B of selling.

Goldman: VIX briefly traded into the 20s on CPI but finished below 20. Goldman reads positioning as a tailwind and the Fed as a headwind. Retail bought the dip with record leveraged ETF inflows of +$3.3B on Thursday and a +$5.7B weekly retail imbalance. Margin debt as a percent of GDP is about 50% above levels where past bubbles popped (~3%).

Morgan Stanley's weekend note ('Shopping') says buy the drop because the market overreacted to the midterms. It estimates about 5 GW of US data center projects, roughly 20% of those slated for 2028, could slip into 2029.
BTIG's Krinsky sees the semis bounce reaching his $150-155 SOXX sell zone, possibly filling the October gap near $169, and would rethink his cautious stance only on a close above $175.

market_movers.rationale: JPMorgan's Harlan Sur cut his target to $215 after removing China from his FY28 estimates. The wrap does not state his rating, so none is asserted here.
JPMorgan's credit team stays Underweight, warning the larger risk is to GPU financing deals where Nvidia acts as supplier, investor or guarantor.
Q3 beat and raise lifted the stock 25% on Wednesday, but guidance includes about $1.1B of quarterly interest expense on $47B of debt.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought $9.7M of stock last week, the second-largest insider purchase in the company's history.
MSCI will remove it from its global equity indexes on Nov 30, which could trigger about $2.8B of stock sales.
Shares fell 2% after Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, aimed at Excel, and Claude Meetings.

sector_views.rationale: Semis rallied on the week, but BTIG sees limited upside above the SOXX $150-155 zone and the Nvidia stock decline reflects a structural shift in the AI trade.
Energy outperformed on the week while rate-sensitive sectors lagged.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3 (reported Tuesday Nov 10): revenue $3.66B vs $3.56B estimate, adjusted EBITDA $2.26B vs $2.05B estimate, adjusted EBITDA margin 62% vs 57.6% estimate. Revenue grew 168%. Adjusted net loss was $529M.
CoreWeave guidance: Q4 interest expense $1.05-1.15B (more than $4B annualized), 2026 capex $35-39B, on $47B of debt.
SoftBank reported a quarterly loss of about $7B versus a $15.6B profit a year earlier. It has borrowed $10B against its OpenAI stake.
Korean chip stocks trade at 2.8x forward earnings, the lowest in 20 years versus a 9.9x average.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter than expected and the trigger for the hike repricing.
Third straight 0.3% month. Waller had said a 50bp hike should be considered at 0.3% or higher.
No annual rate was published in the source, so this is an estimate.
Annual wholesale inflation rose to 6.5%, the highest since 2022.
Pushed 2027 pricing to 50/50 for 2 or 3 more hikes.
A December hike is almost fully priced.
The hike reinforces the global tightening bias.
Up about 27bp on the week, touched 5.17%.
Up 8.4% from the previous year. Higher yields raise costs as debt is refinanced.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell to about $71,400 Thursday (lowest close since mid-August, down almost 6% on the week) and slid below $70,000 Friday, under its 200-day moving average. Ether lost about 10%.
MSCI confirmed it will remove Strategy (MSTR) from its global equity indexes on Nov 30, which could trigger $2.8B of selling. This may partly explain recent bitcoin weakness.
Hyperliquid perpetual futures priced the Huang scandal about 18 hours before Wall Street opened.

trade_ideas.rationale: The bounce has reached the sell zone and BTIG sees little upside beyond a possible fill of the October gap near $169.
trade_ideas.risk: A close above $175 would make BTIG rethink its cautious posture.

trade_ideas.description: Morgan Stanley: buy the drop in equities
trade_ideas.rationale: The market overreacted to the midterms and priced a deeper slowdown than MS forecasts imply.
trade_ideas.risk: AI buildout delays, with about 5 GW of 2028 US data center projects possibly slipping to 2029.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening: a December hike is almost fully priced and a 50bp move is under discussion.
Nvidia leadership uncertainty, the China chip-smuggling investigation and the congressional testimony.
Nvidia's role as a lender, investor or guarantor in GPU financing deals, which JPMorgan credit sees as the larger risk.
AI data center refinancing: $13.4B due starting next year at about 2.85 points higher rates, and $49B owed by CoreWeave and Nebius-type renters from 2030 to 2032.
Leverage: margin debt to GDP at record levels and flash crashes in recent days.
Japanese yen intervention risk at USD/JPY 160.
Credit dispersion: CCC spreads near cycle wides and chip CDS wider than hyperscaler CDS.
MSTR index removal on Nov 30 and bitcoin below its 200-day average.
Weak Treasury auction demand with the 10-year near 5%.

vol_and_positioning: Goldman: VIX briefly traded into the 20s after hot CPI but finished below 20, and the market struggled to sustain a volatility premium. Positioning is a tailwind and the Fed a headwind.
Record +$3.3B leveraged ETF inflows on Thursday and a +$5.7B weekly retail net buy imbalance (+1.1%), per Goldman.
Margin debt as a percent of GDP is at unprecedented levels, about 50% above the ~3% where previous bubbles popped.
Foreign investors put nearly $1.5 trillion into US stocks over the last 12 months, the largest amount on record, per NDR.
The S&P 500 failed at its 100-day moving average Thursday and Friday.
geopolitical: US-Iran: Trump said further strikes were highly unlikely and that he was keeping the status quo. Rubio described a third option of continuing the current approach.

Reports that the US and Iran were considering an $8B deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz were cooled when Trump wrote that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait would prefer the status quo. The blockade remains.
France's Paris prosecutor opened an investigation into Iran as the alleged source of a cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators a month ago.
Smuggled AI chips reportedly reached a Shanghai data center linked to Megaspeed. Commerce Secretary Lutnick agreed to testify before Congress.
Japan's FX chief Mimura warned yen moves were excessively rapid as USD/JPY hit 160.
US midterms were referenced as a driver of the prior market selloff.
cross_bank_references: Goldman had called the yen 'still the best AI hedge' on Monday, then USD/JPY broke 160.
Goldman IG trader Kevin Boova: 'hard to see AA Meta continue to trade at the same levels as low BBB cyclicals without something correcting.'
JPMorgan's equity analyst cut the NVDA target while JPM's credit team stays Underweight.
